subject: Hosted API penetration report access & transfer — encryption key exchange and visibility window
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@acme.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request for latest penetration test report and transfer options

Hi Kimberly,

We're in the middle of an internal SIG review and need the most recent penetration test report for Redwood's Hosted API (production). Could you please share: 1) the latest PT report (redacted if necessary), 2) a brief statement of the test scope (network vs app vs cloud config), and 3) recommended secure transfer mechanisms you support (S3 presigned, SFTP, SFTP+key exchange, secure file portal).

A few constraints from Acme Security: we require access logs for the transfer, a 14-day visibility window on the artifact, and proof of any redactions. If there's an NDA/CDA we need to sign first, please point us to the doc. I've attached a short spreadsheet (Acme-reqs.xlsx) with our checklist.

Thanks — if you can confirm options today that'd help our audit team plan.

— Aisha
Aisha Khan
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
security@acme.com

Attachment: Acme-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet; 28KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request for latest penetration test report and transfer options

Thanks for the clear checklist, Aisha — happy to help. Short answers up front, details below and next steps at the end.

What we can provide today
- Latest PT report (web-app + infra + cloud config coverage) — redacted/high-level version available immediately.
- Full, unredacted report can be shared after a transfer authorization and an exchange of encryption key material; we treat the full report as sensitive.
- Transfer options: presigned S3 (time-limited), managed SFTP with ephemeral account, or secure file portal (third-party vendor with audit logging). We can generate an audit log for any chosen method.

Preferred workflow (recommended for Acme constraints)
1) CDA: sign the attached candidate CDA (cda_template.docx) or confirm your legal prefers their template.
2) Transfer method: managed SFTP with ephemeral account — gives us the best ability to produce timestamped access logs and per-file checksums. Alternatively, presigned S3 links with one-time token are available for up to 72 hours.
3) Key exchange: we support PGP (preferred) or an OOB KMS-based envelope (we can provide a public key or exchange a symmetric key via privileged portal).
4) Visibility window: we can set an access window (recommended 48-72 hours) and provide both the file and a signed access log export.

Attachments I am including: redaction_policy_v2.pdf (internal redaction rules we apply) and transfer_playbook.md (step-by-step for each transfer option). If you pick SFTP I'll ask our infra team to provision an account that auto-expires after the window.

Next steps (suggested)
- Confirm preferred transfer method (SFTP preferred by Acme per your note?).
- If SFTP: confirm the username format you'd like us to use and whether you need SCP or SFTP over port 22 only.
- Legal: confirm whether you will sign our CDA or send your template.
- I will loop Rishi (security) to confirm logging/audit artifacts.

Happy to jump on a quick 15-min call if that's faster.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: redaction_policy_v2.pdf, transfer_playbook.md

Thanks Kimberly — SFTP sounds good. A couple of clarifying items from our side:

- Audit logs: we need a machine-readable access log (CSV or JSON) that includes timestamps, source IP, username, file name, and MD5/SHA256 hashes.
- Account provisioning: prefer ephemeral accounts keyed to our ticketing ID (Zendesk#3421) so we can trace the access back to the request.
- Redaction: if you can provide the redacted PDF now, that will satisfy the SIG review while we finalize the CDA for the unredacted copy.

We'll sign your CDA if it's standard — please send the doc and I'll route it through legal. Once signed, we'll confirm preferred username format (acme_pt_<date> is fine).

Tom from our team will assist with technical verification; tagging him here.

— Aisha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API penetration report access & transfer — encryption key exchange and visibility window

Hi Aisha / Tom — Rishi on Redwood Security. Quick operational plan and confirmation from our side so we can move immediately once CDA is in place.

Operational checklist (what we'll do)
- Provision an ephemeral SFTP account: username pattern acme_pt_20261107_<rand4>. Account auto-deletes after 72 hours.
- Host: sftp.redwood-inference.com (port 22).
- Deliverables placed in /incoming/acme_pt_20261107/ with per-file SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest.
- Access logs: we will provide a CSV audit export with timestamp, source_ip, username, file, and checksum, plus a separate system-generated activity log (JSON) for your SIEM ingestion.
- Key exchange: support PGP — please send a public key to security@redwood.com. If you do not have PGP, we can push a KMS-wrapped symmetric key and you can retrieve it via our portal (we'll provide a one-time passcode).

Legal and scheduling
- Attached is our CDA template (cda_template.docx). If you sign this, we'll proceed same day; if you provide your contract we can accept redlines but will need a short review window (24–48 hours).
- Tentative window: we can target Monday 2026-11-09 08:00–17:00 PST to provision and complete transfer; please confirm if that works for you.

Attachments included for ops: sftp_onboarding_instructions.txt (small checklist) and a copy of the CDA template.

Next steps for Acme
1) Send PGP public key to security@redwood.com or confirm you want KMS route.
2) Sign CDA or provide counter-template.
3) Confirm username pattern and desired transfer window (we proposed Mon 11/09).

If you prefer, we can run a 10-minute verification call during the window to confirm checksums and logs.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
